module.purpose: Provides geometric snapping behavior for translating and resizing editor shapes against nearby shape points and equal-spacing gaps.
module.summary: This module computes page-space snap points and visible horizontal or vertical gaps from editor shapes, then selects nearest point, center-gap, or duplicate-gap matches during movement and resizing. It supports locked axes, aspect-ratio-preserving resize behavior, center resizing, flipped handles, recursive adjacent-gap discovery, duplicate indicator suppression, and generation of visual snap indicators for the snap manager.
module.businessContext: Supports precision layout and alignment in a graphical editor. If it fails, shape movement and resizing lose alignment, spacing, and visual snapping feedback.

detail.name: findAdjacentGaps
detail.signature: function findAdjacentGaps(gaps: Gap[], shapeId: TLShapeId, gapLength: number, direction: 'forward' | 'backward', intersection: [number, number]): Gap[]
preconditions: gaps contains gap records with startNode, endNode, length, and breadthIntersection fields.
direction is either 'forward' or 'backward'.
intersection is a two-number breadth range.
postconditions: Returns every initially matching gap and recursively discovered adjacent matching gap reachable through the selected direction.
A gap matches only when its relevant endpoint shape ID matches, its rounded length equals the rounded requested length, and its breadth intersects the current intersection.
Returns an empty array when no initial gap matches.
invariants: Recursive traversal follows endNode IDs for 'forward' and startNode IDs for 'backward'.
Each next-node ID is traversed at most once during a call.
Gap lengths are compared after applying round to both values.
Breadth intersections are narrowed by intersecting each matched gap with the current intersection.
edgeCases: An empty gaps array returns an empty array.
No gap with the required endpoint, rounded length, and breadth overlap returns an empty array.
A gap whose raw length differs from gapLength but rounds to the same value is treated as a match.
Multiple matching gaps leading to the same next-node ID cause recursive traversal for that node only once.
Gaps with non-overlapping breadth intersections are excluded.
stateMutations: Mutates only local traversal collections; the supplied gaps array and its gap records are not modified.
detail.summary: Finds gaps adjacent to a shape that match the requested length and overlap the requested breadth intersection. It recursively follows matching adjacent gaps in the selected direction while avoiding repeated next nodes.

specLiterals.role: Selects traversal from each gap's start node to its end node.
Selects traversal from each gap's end node to its start node.

specTests.then: The result is an empty array.

specTests.when: findAdjacentGaps is called with direction set to 'forward'.
specTests.then: The matching gap is included in the result, and matching gaps beginning at its endNode.id are recursively included.
That next node is recursively searched at most once.

units.name: dedupeGapSnaps

detail.name: dedupeGapSnaps
preconditions: snaps is an array of gap-type snap indicators.
Each gap exposes startEdge and endEdge as two points with numeric x and y coordinates.
Each snap exposes a direction value and a gaps array.
postconditions: snaps is sorted in descending order by gaps.length.
A snap is removed when an earlier snap with the same direction contains a rounded-coordinate match for every start edge and every end edge in that snap.
Non-redundant snap indicators remain in the array.
invariants: Only snap indicators with matching direction values can deduplicate one another.
Edge-coordinate equality is determined after applying the unit's round helper to each coordinate.
The input array is mutated rather than replaced.
edgeCases: An empty or single-element array is sorted in place and otherwise unchanged.
Snap indicators with different directions are not removed even when all edge coordinates match.
A snap with no gaps satisfies the containment checks and can be removed when a preceding same-direction snap exists.
Duplicate or contained gap indicators are reduced to the preceding, more comprehensive same-direction indicator after descending gap-count sorting.
Coordinates that differ before rounding but match after rounding are treated as equal for deduplication.
stateMutations: The input snaps array is sorted in place and redundant elements are removed from it.
detail.summary: Deduplicates gap snap indicators in place by retaining the more comprehensive indicator when another indicator with the same direction contains all of its rounded edge pairs.

specTests.when: dedupeGapSnaps is called with that array.
specTests.then: The array is sorted with the more comprehensive snap first and the contained snap is removed.
Both snaps remain in the array.

specTests.when: dedupeGapSnaps is called with same-direction snaps.
specTests.then: The less comprehensive snap is treated as redundant and removed.

preconditions: initialSelectionPageBounds is a valid Box.

postconditions: The resize bounds are computed from the initial bounds, handle, drag delta, center-resizing mode, and aspect-ratio mode.
The returned nudge does not move axes locked by the effective resize handle.
Point snapping is evaluated against the manager's snappable points.
When aspect ratio is locked for a corner resize, a non-zero snap nudge is adjusted to preserve the initial selection aspect ratio.
invariants: Negative resize scales flip the effective handle on the corresponding axis before snap-point selection.
For center-based resizing, the drag delta supplied to Box.Resize is doubled on both axes and the resized bounds are recentered on the initial selection bounds.
A top or bottom effective handle locks the x-axis nudge to zero.
A left or right effective handle locks the y-axis nudge to zero.
edgeCases: A resize that produces a negative scale flips the effective handle horizontally and/or vertically before collecting snap points.
Center-based resizing doubles the drag delta and restores the resized bounds center to the initial bounds center.
Aspect-ratio-locked corner resizing with snaps on both axes chooses the axis with the smaller absolute nudge as the primary axis.
If no snap is found on an unlocked axis, the nudge for that axis is zero.
Snapping on an axis locked by the effective handle produces no nudge on that axis.

detail.signature: private collectGapSnaps({ selectionPageBounds, minOffset, nearestSnapsX, nearestSnapsY, }: { selectionPageBounds: Box; minOffset: Vec; nearestSnapsX: NearestSnap[]; nearestSnapsY: NearestSnap[]; })
preconditions: selectionPageBounds contains finite page-coordinate bounds with min/max and center values.
minOffset contains the current minimum allowable snap distances for the x and y axes.
nearestSnapsX and nearestSnapsY are mutable candidate arrays.
postconditions: Visible horizontal and vertical gaps that overlap the selection on their perpendicular axis are evaluated.
nearestSnapsX and nearestSnapsY contain only candidates at the closest rounded offset encountered for their respective axes, subject to the gap-center deduplication rules.
minOffset.x and minOffset.y are updated to the closest absolute offsets encountered for their respective axes.
Center matches are emitted only when the gap is larger than the selection along the matching axis.
Duplication matches record whether the candidate protrudes to the left, right, top, or bottom as applicable.
invariants: A gap is ignored when its breadth intersection does not overlap the selection on the perpendicular axis.
A strictly closer rounded offset clears previously collected candidates for that axis.
Candidates whose rounded offset ties the current minimum are retained.
Gap-center candidates with overlapping breadths suppress the larger overlapping gap in favor of the smaller one.
edgeCases: A gap with no perpendicular-axis overlap produces no snap candidate.
A gap whose length is not greater than the selection dimension produces no center-match candidate, but its duplication matches are still evaluated.
Equal rounded offsets retain multiple candidates rather than selecting only one.
When a closer candidate is found after prior candidates, the corresponding nearest-snap array is cleared before the closer candidate is retained.
Overlapping gap-center candidates retain the smaller gap when the competing center candidate is larger.
stateMutations: Clears and appends to nearestSnapsX and nearestSnapsY.
detail.summary: Collects nearest horizontal and vertical gap-based snap candidates for the selected page bounds. It updates the supplied minimum offsets and candidate arrays in place, including center-alignment and duplicated-spacing snaps.
